title: The Little Shroud
text:
A mother had a little boy of seven who was so lovely that no one could look at him without liking him, and she loved him more than anything in the world. Suddenly he fell ill and died, and she could not be comforted. She wept for him day and night.

Soon after he was buried, the child began to appear at night in the places where he used to sit and play. When his mother wept, he wept too, and when morning came he vanished.

As his mother went on weeping without end, the child came one night in the little white shroud he had been buried in, with the wreath of flowers on his head. He sat on her bed and said, "Oh, Mother, stop crying, or I cannot fall asleep in my coffin. My shroud never dries, because of all your tears that fall on it."

The mother was shocked, and from then on she stopped weeping. The next night the child came again, holding a little candle, and said, "Look, Mother, my shroud is almost dry now, and I can rest in my grave." Then she gave her sorrow to God and bore it quietly and patiently. The child never came again, and slept in his little bed under the earth.
lesson: Love for someone we have lost can, in time, take the form of letting them rest. Moving through grief is not a betrayal of the one we mourn.
source: Brothers Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmarchen, No. 109 (Das Totenhemdchen)
